findings.title: mf_band + sampling_mode='poisson' pairs a plain Poisson sampler with cyclic-Poisson horizon accounting, underreporting epsilon
findings.claim: TrainingArguments explicitly allows privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band' with sampling_mode='poisson' (_training_arguments.py:188 `"mf_band": frozenset({"b_min_sep", "poisson"})`, comment :182 calls it a 'looser-but-valid alternative'), but for that mode build_amplifier_factory constructs the CyclicPoisson horizon accountant (`_ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, BandMfStrategy), sample_rate, n_steps)`, _dpftrl.py:140-154) while build_sampler constructs the plain DP-SGD `PoissonSampler` (_dpftrl.py:224-233, imported from opaque.dpsgd.sampling), not the `CyclicPoissonSampler` the accountant's analysis requires. CyclicPoisson.pld_at charges only `num_groups = ceil(n_steps/bands)` compositions of a Poisson-Gaussian at per-participation sensitivity 1 (_poisson.py:179-188, 214), which is the amplified-BandMF reduction (Choquette-Choo et al. 2023, arXiv:2306.08153) valid only when each example can participate in at most one step per bands-wide window (the cyclic group scheme). Plain Poisson samples every example independently at every one of the n steps (dpsgd/_poisson.py:33-38, _plain_poisson_step_indices), so a record participates ~Binomial(n, q) times with no separation guarantee — both the composition count (n/bands vs ~n effective) and the per-window sensitivity assumption of the accountant are violated. Both mid-run epsilon_at (via per_step -> pld_at(K), _dp_trainer.py:1766, 3960) and noise-multiplier calibration (_dp_trainer.py:4222-4237 -> _calibrate_noise) use this accountant, so the run is calibrated against and reports an epsilon that does not bound the deployed mechanism.
findings.failure_scenario: User sets privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_band' (bands=16 default), sampling_mode='poisson' (passes validation at _training_arguments.py:1048), n=1600 steps, q=0.01, target eps=1. Calibration sizes nm so that ceil(1600/16)=100 Poisson-Gaussian compositions hit eps=1; the deployed run actually gives each record ~16 expected participations across all 1600 steps with possible same-band-window repeats. Measured reference: 100 compositions of poisson(gaussian(1.0), 0.01) give eps(1e-6)=0.954 while the 1600-composition independent-noise reference gives 2.649 — the true epsilon of the deployed banded mechanism under plain Poisson is at least on that order, so the reported/calibrated epsilon is ~2.8x too small at bands=16 and grows with bands. Silent: no warning, training completes, accountant.json records the invalid bound.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:182-188 — '# ``mf_band`` accepts ``"poisson"`` as a looser-but-valid alternative to' ... '"mf_band": frozenset({"b_min_sep", "poisson"})'; validation at :1048 only checks membership in this set.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:138-154 — sampling_mode=='poisson' returns `_ftrl_poisson(mf_gaussian(nm, _s), sample_rate=_sr, n_steps=_ns, ...)` with _s = the BandMfStrategy; _dpftrl.py:224-233 — same mode returns `PoissonSampler(dataset, sample_rate=sample_rate, n_steps=n_steps, ...)`.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:179-188,214 — BandMF branch: `rounded = min(-(-n_steps // bands) * bands, self.n_steps); num_groups = math.ceil(rounded / bands)` then `per_group_pld.self_compose(num_groups)`; module docstring :3-7 states the analysis divides the run into `num_groups = ceil(n_steps / bands)` independent groups — a property of the cyclic scheme, not of plain Poisson.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/sampling/_poisson.py:43-56 — CyclicPoissonSampler is the sampler that implements the accounted scheme ('Step i samples only from group i % bands'); build_sampler only constructs it for sampling_mode='cyclic_poisson', which is NOT in _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS for any mechanism.
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_poisson.py:33-38 — PoissonSampler: 'Each example is independently included with probability sample_rate' at every step; no band separation.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:3675-3684 — stale comment claims 'poisson' is only reachable for 'DP-SGD + mf_identity', contradicting _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS; and CyclicPoisson.min_sep docstring (_poisson.py:87-94) concedes 'any example could in principle be sampled on consecutive rounds' while the PLD still prices ceil(n/bands) groups.

Measured (this session, .venv python): (poisson(gaussian(1.0),0.01)*100).epsilon_at(1e-6)=0.9542 vs (*1600)=2.6495; BandMfStrategy.sensitivity(n_steps=N)=1.0 exactly (coefficients L2-normalized, _toeplitz.py optimize returns params/norm), so effective_nm == nm and the accountant is exactly the 100-fold composition.

Not tracked: grep of issues-open.tsv shows only #699 'Tighten partial-band prefixes for CyclicPoisson with BandMF' (a tightening issue, not this sampler/accountant mismatch); AUDIT-master-list.md has no finding on this pairing; the pairing predates the delta (present at 79c916e3) but feeds the new horizon-prefix machinery and was never flagged.
findings.fix_sketch: Either drop 'poisson' from _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS['mf_band'] (fail-closed), or make build_sampler construct CyclicPoissonSampler(bands=mf.strategy.bands) when the mechanism is mf_band and sampling_mode=='poisson' so the runtime matches the CyclicPoisson accountant (and audit the sample_rate/group-size convention against the amplified-BandMF theorem while doing so). Also fix the stale reachability comment at _dp_trainer.py:3675-3684.

findings.title: BallsInBins.pld_at docstring claims K-epoch reparameterization for BSR/BiSR/lambda-CGD and carries an unreachable BLT pinned-prefix gram branch
findings.claim: The pld_at docstring (:150-152) states 'For horizon-independent inners (Identity, BSR, BiSR, lambda-CGD) the gram / primitive is reparameterised by K_epochs = rounded // num_bins' and describes an N-pinned BLT prefix gram (:152-156), but the guard at :181 (`if not isinstance(s, IdentityStrategy) and rounded < self.n_steps: return self.pld_at(self.n_steps, ...)`) snaps EVERY non-Identity prefix to the full-horizon PLD. Consequently the BLT pinned-coefficient branch (:216-235) and the BSR/BiSR/lambda-CGD `gram_matrix(n_steps=rounded)` branch (:236-244) only ever execute with rounded == self.n_steps, where they reproduce the full-horizon gram — the prefix differentiation they implement is dead code. The docstring's last two sentences (:156-158) then correctly state the opposite ('Correlated-strategy Monte Carlo paths use the full-horizon confidence bound for every nonzero prefix'), so the docstring contradicts itself. Behavior is conservative (full-horizon PLD dominates any prefix by post-processing over the causal streaming transcript), so this is not a privacy defect; it is a maintenance trap: a future edit trusting the first half of the docstring (or reviving the dead branch without re-deriving its validity) would change prefix pricing silently.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor implementing open issues #694/#696/#698/#700 (tighten BnB prefixes) reads :150-156, concludes the K-epoch gram path is already live and tested, and deletes the :181 guard — activating the never-exercised gram-at-rounded path (including the BLT coefs[:rounded] slice, whose validity as a bound was never established for K < N) without any test noticing, since no test can currently reach those branches with rounded < n_steps.
evidence: _balls_in_bins.py:181-191 — early return to pld_at(self.n_steps) for every non-Identity strategy with rounded < n_steps.
_balls_in_bins.py:216-235 — `if isinstance(s, BltStrategy): ... pinned = list(coefs[:rounded].tolist())` — only reachable when rounded == self.n_steps, so coefs[:rounded] is always the whole column.
_balls_in_bins.py:150-152 vs :156-158 — the same docstring asserts both K-epoch reparameterization and full-horizon-for-every-prefix.
Open issues #694/#696/#698/#700 track tightening these prefixes (behavioral softness is tracked); the in-code self-contradiction and dead differentiation are not mentioned in any open issue title.
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the pld_at docstring to describe the shipped behavior only (Identity: exact per-epoch prefix; everything else: full-horizon bound), and either delete the dead BLT/BSR prefix-gram differentiation or gate it behind the future tightening work with tests that actually reach it.

findings.title: accounting.md documents a 'hypergeometric prefix mixture' for k_out_of_t that the Python surface never computes
findings.claim: docs/user-guide/accounting.md:180-183 states for `dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t`: 'pld_at(K) accounts the hypergeometric prefix mixture; the full k>1 PLD uses the conservative Feldman-Shenfeld block reduction.' In the shipped code, KOutOfT.pld_at (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_k_out_of_t.py:93-107) snaps every k>1 prefix (n_steps < self.n_steps and total_participations > 1) to the full-horizon block bound, and for k==1 the Rust entry point delegates to the exact 1-out-of-t allocation prefix before any hypergeometric weight is computed (random_allocation.rs:293-299). The hypergeometric-cap path (random_allocation.rs:301-330) is unreachable from the Python API — the KOutOfT docstring itself (:28-33) and the Rust doc comment (:266-270, 'the Python wrapper snaps k>1 prefix queries to the full-horizon block bound instead') say so. Verified numerically: k_out_of_t(gaussian(1.0), total_participations=2, n_steps=8) returns identical epsilon (4.76621 at delta=1e-6) for pld_at(1), pld_at(3), pld_at(7), and pld_at(8). The reported number remains a valid upper bound, but the doc promises a materially tighter mid-run epsilon than the library delivers, which misleads early-stopping/budget decisions.
findings.failure_scenario: A user plans a k=4-of-1000 run expecting mid-run epsilon to grow gradually per the documented hypergeometric prefix accounting, budgets eps=2 for a possible early stop at K=250, and finds (or worse, doesn't check and their budget monitor trips immediately) that epsilon_at reports the full-horizon value from step 1 onward.
evidence: docs/user-guide/accounting.md:180-183 — 'pld_at(K) accounts the hypergeometric prefix mixture'.
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_k_out_of_t.py:93-107 — `if n_steps < self.n_steps and self.total_participations > 1: ... return self.pld_at(self.n_steps, ...)`.
packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:266-270 — 'the Python wrapper snaps k > 1 prefix queries to the full-horizon block bound instead'.
Measured (this session): KOutOfT(k=2, n=8) epsilon at K in {1,3,7,8} all equal 4.76621 at delta=1e-6.
Open issue #693 ('Derive a prefix PLD for K-out-of-T with multiple participations') tracks building the tight prefix; it does not cover the user guide asserting that the tight prefix already exists.
findings.fix_sketch: Change accounting.md:180-183 to state that k>1 prefixes conservatively return the full-horizon block bound (matching the KOutOfT docstring), and mention the exact k=1 prefix path; update once #693 lands.

clean_areas: random_allocation_gaussian_prefix_pld (random_allocation.rs:194-251): re-derived the released-prefix dominating pair by hand — P_r = (r/t)*P_bar_r + ((t-r)/t)*Q^r decomposed into the pmf_q / pmf_active mixture with weights (1-r/t, r/t), the neg-dual e^{l under Q} identity for the Gaussian, the add-direction e^{-L} symmetry, and the add_constant(t-r) terms all match the exact prefix law; rounding directions (Up on remove path, Down on the inner add-side sum then Up on -ln) are all conservative. Verdict: exact and safe.

RandomAllocation.pld_at (dpsgd/_random_allocation.py:110-161): full-epoch self-compose + exact partial-epoch prefix verified against the runtime RandomAllocationSampler semantics (assignment redrawn per epoch, _random_allocation.py sampler docstring:11-13); epsilon monotone over K=1..20 with num_bins=5 measured numerically (no violations at 1e-12 tolerance).

KOutOfT prefix: k=1 exact prefix monotone over K=1..16 (measured); k>1 prefixes snap to the full-horizon block bound, which is a valid upper bound for any released prefix by post-processing (allocation is drawn upfront, per-step noise is independent, so the K-prefix is a marginal of the full transcript). The Rust k>1 hypergeometric-cap path is unreachable from Python (only affects direct native callers), and the block-decomposition upper bound's symmetry + joint-convexity argument (random_allocation.rs:400-414) was re-derived and is sound (uniform random equal-block partition + one pick per block induces the uniform k-subset distribution by transitive symmetry).

CyclicPoisson.pld_at (dpftrl/_poisson.py:142-214): BandMF prefix = ceil(K/bands) per-group compositions with N-evaluated sensitivity; verified numerically that pld_at(3) with bands=2 equals poisson_gaussian_pld(nm/sens, q).self_compose(2) exactly and that epsilon is monotone with band-boundary plateaus; BandMfStrategy.sensitivity == 1.0 by construction (optimize() L2-normalizes, _toeplitz.py:692), which is the correct per-participation column norm for the amplified-BandMF reduction, and the K-prefix is the first ceil(K/b) cycles of that reduction — valid WHEN the cyclic sampler is used (see finding 1 for the trainer pairing that breaks this).

BallsInBins Identity prefix (_balls_in_bins.py:205-214): the sigma/sqrt(K_epochs) collapse onto 1-out-of-b random allocation re-derived from the Lemma 3.2 gram G = E*I_b (fixed bins => same slot every epoch => sufficient-statistic mean); measured epsilon over K=1..12 (num_bins=4): monotone, plateaus within epochs, partial-epoch round-up conservative, pld_at(n_steps) == pld() exactly. nm==0 fail-closed to non_private_pld.

Correlated BnB and BMinSep prefixes (_balls_in_bins.py:181-191, _b_min_sep/__init__.py:144-155): every nonzero prefix returns the full-horizon (confidence-bounded MC) PLD — conservative for the released transcript because streaming noise generation is causal, so the K-prefix is a marginal of the N-step transcript and post-processing applies; trivially monotone in K. Tightening tracked by open #694-#700; no invalidity found.

per_step/Repeated/Cached wiring: verified by execution that Repeated(per_step(p), K).epsilon_at == p.pld_at(K).epsilon_at, that an Accountant loop of 5 `| step` merges into the same value, and that composing beyond the declared horizon raises ValueError (fail-closed, _per_step.py:61-66). CachedProcess relays repeated_pld to its inner (fix #290 intact, _cached.py:88-109), iter_cache_key propagates Repeated.count as the leaf's n_steps and passes through CachedProcess (_iter_cache_key.py:28-35), and horizon_pld_cache keys include the raw n_steps argument (_pld_cache.py:242) so the BLT constant-per-prefix _pld_cache_key (BallsInBins:_pld_cache_key:117-119) cannot collide across prefixes; all five families' _pld_cache_key contents were checked complete against their PLD inputs (nm, bins/bands, horizon, p0/sample_rate, materialized lr schedules via strategy_cache_key).

Monotonicity of epsilon in prefix length: checked numerically for RandomAllocation (K=1..20, partial epochs), KOutOfT k=1 (K=1..16), BallsInBins Identity (K=1..12), CyclicPoisson BandMF (K=1..8); correlated BnB/BMinSep/KOutOfT-k>1 are constant in K by construction. No non-monotone prefix bound found, so the early-stopping exploit surface (report a lower epsilon by stopping at a dip) is closed for the shipped families.

Mid-run epsilon semantics: for all five horizon families, epsilon_at after K composed steps prices either the exact released K-prefix (RandomAllocation, KOutOfT k=1, CyclicPoisson, BnB Identity) or the planned-horizon bound (correlated BnB, BMinSep, KOutOfT k>1), i.e., always an upper bound on the released transcript; no fail-open direction found. predict_stop_step (_dp_trainer.py:272-333) binary search is guarded by an explicit boundary-monotonicity check and MC accountants are excluded by the sampling-mode gate at _dp_trainer.py:1176; the constant-prefix pessimistic-stop behavior for MC accountants is tracked open #688.

cached() horizon guards (_cached.py:164-209): Accountant/DpProcess trees containing a DpHorizonProcess are skipped with a warning instead of freezing a stale PLD barrier; _contains_horizon_process walks Composed/Repeated/Cached/PerStep correctly (checked all four node types); bare PerStep is cached as a merge-barrier whose repeated_pld still reaches pld_at. Continuation-across-runs semantics for correlated processes remain open (#683/#685) — not re-reported.

BnB Monte Carlo upper-confidence construction direction (balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:335-410, commit 88a25769/#748): order-statistic KL lower-CDF band pushes uncertified mass to infinity_mass, producing a stochastically dominating PLD — direction is conservative; per-query failure-probability splitting across Composed groups (_composed.py:68-88) and calibration probes (calibration.py:298-303) checked. Deep numerical certification of the MC internals is tracked open #697 and was not re-audited.
